sections.text: For Thou art the Father of all things movable and immovable, the Worshipful, the Master of Masters! In all the worlds there is none equal to Thee, how then superior, O Thou who standeth alone, Supreme.

Therefore I prostrate myself before Thee, O Lord! Most Adorable! I salute Thee, I ask Thy blessing. Only Thou canst be trusted to bear with me, as father to son, as friend to friend, as lover to his beloved.
I rejoice that I have seen what never man saw before; yet, O Lord! I am overwhelmed with fear. Please take again the Form I know. Be merciful, O Lord! thou Who are the Home of the whole universe.

As we have been discussing last few times, that now that Arjuna has seen this cosmic form of the Lord, in other words, his mind has comprehended the unity of this plurality, this world which seemingly is divided among this plurality of things and beings, is actually strung by the same entity which manifests as this plurality, beings and things come out of the same reality and dissolve into the same reality. That reality is what hes facing right now. So hes now offering his prayer, his adoration to that.
And he has said, you are everything -- Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna. Anything that I can think of, any being my mind can perceive, is nothing but you alone; all I see is you. And therefore he says, my salutations to you, my salutations to you a thousand times.
I salute you from your front, I salute you in your back, I salute you at your side, because you are everywhere. Wherever I turn around, I see you. If we come to the conclusion that this world is nothing but the Lords manifestation, then obviously when we turn around, we see him.
Just like this classical story -- maybe its folklore -- that Nanak went to Kaaba and was sleeping with his feet towards Kaaba. The Maulvi comes and says, you idiot, what are you doing? He said, oh, is that what Im doing? Well, then move my leg to where the Kaaba is not. The Maulvi in anger moves his leg.
Wherever he turns it, he sees Kaaba moving around with it. So basically saying God is everywhere, because God is everything, therefore God is everywhere. So he said, therefore.
Now, whatever I see when I say I bow down in the front, in the back and the rear, whatever I see in front of me, whatever I see in the side of me is nothing. But you and I recognize that in our culture we say namaste -- Namah te -- I bow down to you. Not you as a person, but you the self, which is no other than myself.
Once we find that commonality, we obviously cant have animosity or jealousy. But we just give lip service. Namaste -- we never understood.
So obviously we dont get the benefit of that. But if we develop any commonality with anybody -- somebody says, Sunil, which university did you go to? Oh, Im also from Baroda. Then we start feeling comfortable right there. Then he says, Which year were you? The more we find we have in common, the more we like each other, the more we fall in love with each other.
In other words, we find more identification with that person. So here now he is finding that everything that he knows is now him. So he is offering his salutation.
Then he suddenly realizes that maybe when he was not aware of this fact, he may have insulted people. He may have insulted people who he should actually be respecting. In this case, obviously, he superimposes all of that onto Krishna, because Krishna is the one who showed him this Vishwaroop.
So he identifies what he is seeing as Krishnas self. I, Arjuna, am seeing Krishnas self as this great cosmic being who is everywhere and everything. Therefore, Hare Ram Hare Krishna -- which is Prabhupadas movement -- they call it Krishna consciousness.
The lineage from Shankaracharya speaks of consciousness, self-consciousness. Myself and yourself is one and the same. Prabhupada comes from a different lineage, which is a dualistic school of thought.
They look at the Bhagavad Gita the same way except with a slightly different twist: they will say, let my consciousness right now -- ego consciousness -- identify with the Krishna consciousness. Then I become one with Krishna, the Krishna, not that historical Krishna but the universal being. So here Arjuna sees the same way as this is the Krishnas great cosmic form.
I have known Krishna from my childhood as Devakis son, Yashodas son, my cousin -- but look at his greatness. Sakha Ithimatva Prasabham Yad Uktam -- not knowing your greatness, I may have addressed you disrespectfully. This may not be appropriate for a great being like you.
When I came to this country, this was the biggest problem I had. Here, everybody called everybody by first name. Obviously, I was trained in India.
And I said, Oh, Rajan, you can call.. I say, hes the president of our company of 200 people. I am not going to call him David. No, no, its okay, call him David. But very difficult for us to do that -- how can I say? Even today, after living here for 30 years, I have a client named Charles McFarlane, and obviously we call him Charles. Hes about my age, so much younger than me.
His father is 80-something and he used to be our senator, Granger McFarlane. But hes also part of this project which Im doing. So Charles will say, Call my father. Everybody called him Granger.
I said, Im not going to do that. I call him Mr. McFarlane and call Charles, Charles.
Thats how I make the distinction. So now Arjuna, realizing this, says, I must have done something not right -- I called you Sakha. So ajanata mahimanam avedam -- not that I want to disrespect you, but I did not know your greatness, that you are that all-pervading being.
See, till we come to see God, we are not one with him, and therefore we always say, Oh God, you are so almighty. We never say, O my own self, which is almighty. Because who is seeking this relief from pain and unhappiness? Actually, the sufferer right now is none other than my ego. Something happens -- who gets hurt? So who needs liberation? My ego can never be the Gods self. So my ego says oh forgive me Lord.
So here Arjuna says, O forgive me. In not knowing your greatness, I must have called you Sakha, Yadava, Krishna, whatever. Maya pramadat pranayana vapi -- pramadat, out of my lethargy in understanding you.
I could have realized what Im realizing today had I given enough thought to it. But it never occurred to me that I should put enough effort to know you. So pramada pranayana vapya -- therefore I must have done this thing out of love for you.
I liked you, I loved you. I just did not know your greatness. Therefore I could not give you the due respect which you deserve.
Just continuing that -- Yacha avaha sartham asat krutosi vihara sayya asana bhujanesho -- while we were together, roaming around, sleeping in the same room, eating dinner, whatever, eating things together, I must have done things disrespectfully to you. Eko athwa api achyuta tat tamaksam tat kshamaye tvam aham aprameyam -- or when we were just alone, I must have done that. So he says, in any situation -- hes just enumerating what situations he must have done this in, whether in company or when they were together with other people.
Sometimes I say oh, its okay that you insulted me because nobody was here. Thats not good that you did that in front of my friend. Maybe I did it alone.
But I may have done it even in front of other people. All of the tat shamaye. Please forgive me O Aapramayyam.
Because you are immeasurable. Basically, when an individual recognizes the Lords greatness, in a sense we come to recognize that we are powerless in this world. And everything that we have achieved is because of his presence.
Then all the credit we have taken, the ego we have developed -- all that, we feel so bad about it. I must have done all of this, O Lord, out of my own ignorance. But please forgive me.
Then he says why the Lord should forgive him. Let me tell you why you should forgive me. Because I know and I now recognize that you are Pitasi Lokasyachara Acharasya.
You are the father of this entire Jagat made up of chara and Achara. That means everything. Then nothing you can leave behind in it.
You are the most respectful, worshipable Guru Gariyan. You are the greatest teacher of all. I did not know all this.
You may take some blame for that -- you are the greatest guru, and living with you, I still didnt learn all this. But you are the father of all the beings. Na tvat samo asti abhyadhikah.
There is no one greater than you. I now recognize your almighty power. I thought he is powerful and he is powerful and she is powerful, and I was running after them.
But I realized, when I divide this world into plurality again -- none of them have independent power. You are the powerhouse of everything. In these three worlds.
These three worlds can be defined in many different ways. One is obviously Swarga Lok, Patal Lok, and this Lok -- or Swarga, Nark, and Prithvi Lok. But three Lokas generally in Vedanta mean: my waking world is one world, in which I have all these people who are more powerful than I am, and Im trying to gain their favor.
Im trying to be in their company. Anytime we see somebody -- the president comes, everybody says, Mr. President, very glad to see you, sir. The president says, Very glad to see you also. He moves on because there are 5,000 people in a day he probably tells that to.
We put the picture in our office. Rajan with Obama. Obama probably doesnt care. There are thousands of pictures like that. Pretty close relationship. We all have pictures with. We were very close to. Was close to us? But thats our ego basically tells us to do. But this also our way of showing respect.
There is none greater than you. So in my waking world I have thought there are many. But none has power of their own.
They all derive power from you. So you are the greatest of all in my waking world. Same is true for my dream world.
I derive power in my dream world because I am conscious. I am self aware in my dream. And my own mind creates my own world.
Even there, none greater than you. And when Im in deep sleep, there is no one. Im completely ignorant.
In my deep sleep there is no thought. In deep sleep, you are the only one who takes care of me at the time. None greater than in these three worlds.
In the last verse we see Tasmad -- therefore. Pranamya Pranidhaya Kayam -- therefore I bow down, bending my body. Prasadaye Tvam Aham Isham Idyam -- seeking your forgiveness, O adorable Lord.
Now knowing your greatness, I adore you. We have learned what adoration is. Intensive form of love.
Intensive love is intense identification. I am now bowing down to you with my body, with my mind, and with my intellect. Pita Eva Putrasya -- just as the father forgives his son, no matter what the son does, once he says, Dad, Im sorry, thats the end of the story.
No matter how bad it was. Okay my son, dont do it ever again. But Im letting you go.
And son knows that that trick works all the time. He said, because theres a love between the father and the son. No matter what it is, he forgives you.
So you should do that. You are the father of the whole universe. Thats another relationship where forgiveness comes very easy.
You and your friend are really mad at each other. And the other friend, you know, Rajan, Im so sorry I did that. Thats the end of the story.
Lets go see a movie together. Its a very different relationship. And then when youre in love, when somebody is beloved to you, no matter what differences you have.
And youre mad at each other, as soon as one person says, Im sorry, thats the end of the story.

Arjuna appeals to three relationships where forgiveness comes naturally: as father to son, as friend to friend, as lover to his beloved. Then he makes his request: I rejoice that I have seen what never man saw before; yet I am overwhelmed with fear. Please take again the Form I know. He asks to see Krishna with the crown, the sceptre and the discus - the familiar four-armed Vishnu form he grew up venerating. The cosmic vision, while revelatory, is more than he can bear.
This reveals something important about spiritual growth: we can only integrate as much truth as we are prepared to hold. Arjunas request is not weakness but wisdom - he knows his limits. The cosmic vision showed him ultimate reality, but he needs to return to a form he can relate to, worship, and live with. Similarly, moments of profound spiritual insight often need to be followed by integration into ordinary life.
Reflect today on your own capacity to hold truth. Have you had experiences or insights that were overwhelming? How did you integrate them? Notice the balance between reaching for expanded awareness and respecting your current capacity. What gentle form of the divine can you relate to in daily life? What practice or image or relationship helps you connect with the sacred in a sustainable way? Honor both the aspiration for ultimate truth and the need for forms that support your current stage of development.
